thesis: Docusign's confirmed fiscal Q2 2027 result showed revenue of $875.7 million, up 9% year over year including about 1.3 percentage points of foreign-exchange benefit, and management increased full-year revenue, ARR-growth, and IAM-mix guidance. The strongest counter-evidence is still-modest, partly currency-assisted growth plus the active Mistwood patent case, whose Markman hearing is scheduled for December 11, 2026; the raised outlook and expanding IAM mix keep the net read positive, but the scheduled hearing requires active_litigation and therefore low conviction. Current filings show earlier securities and related opt-out cases were dismissed or closed, and this run found no qualifying governance-history event.
invalidation: Management cuts the raised outlook, IAM adoption fails to support recurring growth, cash conversion deteriorates materially, or the December patent claim-construction hearing materially increases expected legal exposure.

thesis: Samsara's confirmed fiscal Q2 2027 result showed revenue of $508.4 million and ending ARR of $2.125 billion, both up 30% year over year, while issuer-reported operating income turned positive at $4.9 million. The strongest counter-evidence is that $101.1 million of quarterly stock-based-compensation-related charges remains large relative to operating income and full-year revenue guidance implies 26% growth, below the quarter's pace; sustained 30% ARR growth, 28% net-new-ARR growth, and positive reported operating income keep the net read positive despite that dilution and deceleration concern. The latest filing describes ordinary-course litigation without a scheduled adverse event in the next roughly 90 days, and this run found no qualifying governance-history event.
invalidation: ARR or revenue growth decelerates materially below the current outlook, large-customer expansion weakens, reported operating profitability reverses without a temporary explanation, or stock-based compensation rises faster than operating leverage.

thesis: Frontline's confirmed Q2 2026 result reported record quarterly profit of $659.2 million on $943.3 million of revenue, with issuer-reported per-share earnings of $2.96 under IAS 34 interim reporting, alongside exceptionally strong realized tanker rates. The completed sale of two VLCCs also supported a declared $0.80 special dividend in addition to the regular Q2 dividend. The strongest counter-evidence is that tanker spot rates are cyclical and the asset-sale dividend is explicitly one-time; record realized charter earnings and lower financing margins support the positive read, but the thesis depends on operating cash generation rather than treating the special distribution as recurring. This run found no scheduled litigation event or qualifying governance-history event.
invalidation: Realized tanker rates fall sharply, fleet utilization or operating cash generation deteriorates, financing costs reverse higher, or capital returns become dependent on repeated asset sales rather than operations.
sources: Frontline 2026 half-year report filed with the SEC: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/913290/000162828026062234/fro-20260630.htm

thesis: Akamai disclosed signed project plans supporting an $11.6 billion, seven-year cloud-services commitment from Anthropic, with potential expansion of up to another $9 billion. The strongest counter-evidence is approximately $5.5 billion of related capital spending, no expected impact to 2026 revenue guidance, termination provisions, and a warrant whose conversion can represent up to about 5% of common shares; the contracted demand supports a positive long-term read, but the newly issued warrant requires dilution_risk and therefore low conviction. The latest quarterly filing characterizes current legal matters as routine and not expected to be material, and this run found no qualifying governance-history event.
invalidation: Anthropic reduces or terminates the commitment, deployment economics or cash generation fall materially short, required capital rises beyond disclosed estimates, or warrant-linked dilution expands without commensurate contracted revenue.

thesis: BOXX's near-52-week-high signal is consistent with its mechanical objective of producing short-duration, Treasury-bill-like returns through option box spreads rather than a company-specific catalyst. The fund reported a 4.06% one-year NAV return through August 31, 2026, and its September holdings were overwhelmingly offsetting SPY option legs. The strongest counter-evidence is derivative, counterparty, tax, and implementation risk plus the absence of a fundamental catalyst; those risks do not negate its cash-reserve role, but the mechanical nature of the signal requires low conviction. This run found no qualifying scheduled litigation, governance-history, dilution, liquidity, or leadership-turnover flag.
invalidation: NAV behavior stops tracking a stable short-duration accrual pattern, option-spread implementation or counterparty exposure becomes impaired, expenses materially erode the intended return, or tax or regulatory changes undermine the structure.
sources: Alpha Architect BOXX fund page and holdings: https://funds.alphaarchitect.com/boxetf/
EA Series Trust annual shareholder report: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1592900/000159290025004114/ck0001592900-20250930.htm
